disclaimer: Simplified statutory baselines for scheduling guidance only — not legal advice. Laws change and many countries vary by state/province, sector, award or collective agreement. Verify with local counsel and adjust the values to your agreements.

laws.name: India
laws.source: Factories Act 1948 ss. 51, 54–56, 59 (state Shops & Establishments Acts vary)
laws.notes: No more than 5 hours' work without a rest interval of at least 30 minutes; spread-over limited to 10.5 hours. Many states' Shops & Establishments Acts set their own limits.

laws.name: United States (federal)
laws.notes: Federal law sets weekly overtime after 40 hours but no daily limit or mandatory breaks. Many states add meal/rest-break and daily-overtime rules — pick the state preset where available.

laws.name: United States — California
laws.source: California Labor Code § 512; IWC Wage Orders (meal periods)
laws.notes: 30-minute meal period before the end of the 5th hour, a second after 10 hours (waivers possible). Paid 10-minute rest breaks per 4 hours are not checked here. Daily overtime after 8 hours.

laws.name: United Kingdom
laws.notes: Uninterrupted 20-minute break when working more than 6 hours; 11 hours' daily rest (so at most a 13-hour working day); 48-hour average week unless opted out. Young workers have stricter limits.

laws.name: Germany
laws.notes: 8 hours a day, extendable to 10 if averaged back to 8. Breaks of 30 min after 6 h and 45 min after 9 h, taken in blocks of at least 15 min; no more than 6 hours without a break; 11 hours' rest.

laws.name: France
laws.notes: Legal week of 35 hours (overtime beyond); at most 10 hours a day and 48 a week; a 20-minute break once 6 hours are worked; 11 hours' daily rest. Collective agreements often differ.

laws.name: Spain
laws.notes: Up to 9 ordinary hours a day (unless agreed otherwise); a 15-minute break when the continuous working day exceeds 6 hours; 12 hours between working days.

laws.name: Philippines
laws.notes: 8 normal hours a day with overtime beyond; a regular meal period of at least 60 minutes (shorter only in specific cases). Applied here to shifts of more than 5 worked hours — a simplification.

laws.name: Canada (federal)
laws.source: Canada Labour Code Part III ss. 169, 169.1, 171
laws.notes: Federally regulated employers: 8/40 standard hours, 48-hour weekly maximum, a 30-minute break every 5 consecutive hours and 8 hours' rest between shifts. Provinces set their own rules.

laws.name: Australia
laws.source: Fair Work Act 2009 s. 62 (NES); breaks set by modern awards
laws.notes: 38-hour week plus reasonable additional hours. Meal breaks come from the applicable modern award — a 30-minute unpaid meal break within 5 hours is typical but varies.

laws.name: Singapore
laws.notes: For employees covered by Part IV: no more than 6 consecutive hours without a period of leisure, at most 12 hours a day including overtime, 72 overtime hours a month. Break length shown is a simplification — verify.

laws.name: United Arab Emirates
laws.notes: 8 hours a day / 48 a week; overtime of no more than 2 hours a day; no more than 5 consecutive hours without breaks totalling at least 1 hour. Reduced hours apply in Ramadan.

laws.name: Brazil
laws.source: Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) arts. 58, 59, 66, 71
laws.notes: 8 hours a day / 44 a week, overtime of at most 2 hours a day; a 15-minute break for 4–6 hour days and at least 1 hour for longer days (reducible by collective agreement); 11 hours between days.

laws.name: Mexico
laws.notes: 8-hour day shift / 48-hour week; overtime of at most 3 hours a day, 3 times a week; a rest of at least 30 minutes during a continuous working day (applied here to days over 6 hours — a simplification).

laws.name: South Africa
laws.source: Basic Conditions of Employment Act ss. 9, 10, 14, 15
laws.notes: 45-hour week (9 hours a day on a 5-day week); overtime of at most 3 hours a day / 10 a week; a 1-hour meal interval after 5 hours' continuous work (reducible to 30 minutes by agreement); 12 hours' daily rest.
